findings.issue:
Regression for proxied curl. `pypi.rs` runs `curl -sS -i`, and with HTTPS_PROXY set curl -i prints the proxy's CONNECT reply before the real response. That reply often carries headers, for example `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
Proxy-agent: Squid

HTTP/2 404 ...`. The new skip rule `(status < 200 || headers.is_empty()) && body.starts_with("HTTP/")` does not skip that block: its status is 200 and it has a header. The parser then returns status 200 with the whole real response, status line included, as the body, so a real 404 or 429 is misread as 200 with an unparseable body. The old code took the last status line, so it handled this case, and the old doc comment promised it. No test covers a preamble that has headers.
findings.fix: Skip any block whose body starts with `HTTP/`, whatever its status or headers, with `if body.starts_with("HTTP/") { rest = body; continue; }`. A JSON or HTML body never starts with a status line, and the condition gets simpler. Add one test with a CONNECT 200 preamble that has a `Proxy-agent` header, followed by a 404.

findings.issue: The existing test `a_response_is_split_at_the_last_header_block_and_keeps_its_headers` is now misnamed. The parser splits at the first blank line, so the name describes the behavior this change removed.
findings.fix: Rename it to describe the current behavior, for example `a_response_keeps_its_status_headers_and_body`.

findings.issue: The changeset says "forge responses", but the same parser also reads the PyPI simple-index responses fetched with curl in `registry/pypi.rs`. Users of registry checks are affected too and will not recognise themselves in "forge".
findings.fix: Name both: "Release and registry lookups no longer fail when a GitHub or PyPI response body contains a blank line."
